offered.abstract: Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

offered.title: The Symmetry of Differential Neural Tangent Kernel under the Orthogonal Group
offered.abstract: The differential neural tangent kernel (DNTK) is a tool for analyzing the training dynamics of overparameterized physics informed neural networks. In this work, we investigate the symmetry of the infinite DNTK under an orthogonal group, for two layer and deep neural networks separately, based on the explicit expression of the DNTK and recursive formula, respectively. The results are for all activations with or without a bias term, and shed insight into the structure of the infinite width DNTK. Then we prove that the integral operators over the unit sphere induced by operators from the same group orbit share the spectrum, and their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and that the operator fixed DNTK exhibits zonal symmetry on the unit sphere for symmetric operators. Thus the eigenvalue decay rate of the associated integral operator can be derived for shallow networks with RePU activation and zero bias initialization.

offered.title: Lie Symmetry-Guided Adaptive Sampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), with broad applications in physics, engineering, and medicine. However, their performance is highly sensitive to the sampling strategy for training points. Conventional uniform sampling often fails to adequately resolve regions with complex solution features, leading to low efficiency and limited accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a Lie symmetry-driven adaptive sampling framework for PINNs, termed Lie-AS-ISC. For PDEs admitting Lie symmetry groups, symmetry transformations are exploited to derive intrinsic functional relationships between the solution and its variables, enabling the construction of basis points with exact solutions that span the solution domain. Building on this, an adaptive sampling strategy is developed by jointly considering absolute error and invariant surface conditions, while a dual-index loss is introduced to enhance training constraints. The proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy. The experimental results show that this method consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy.

offered.title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
offered.abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.

overviews.overview: This period’s PINN papers pushed hardest on regimes with sharp gradients, discontinuities, or inverse identification. In semiconductor drift-diffusion, a PINN handled an abrupt PN junction in one and two dimensions, with extreme carrier gradients and a discontinuous doping profile, and matched commercial TCAD accuracy across all observables and bias conditions while also tackling doping retrieval [2610.33133]. In bubbly-liquid acoustics, a KdVB-PINN paired forward solving with sensitivity analysis over eight parameters; seven single-parameter inversions gave 0.8–2.1% errors for five parameters, one converged only partially, and surface tension was unidentifiable [2610.32668]. In self-gravitating turbulence, PINNs tracked 2D/3D turbulent molecular clouds over multiple free-fall times, with training cost rising by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 [2610.32840].

picks.hook: Best starting point if you care about PINNs in device physics: it shows a hard-constrained solver coping with abrupt junctions, extreme carrier gradients, and inverse doping recovery under all bias conditions.

Worth reading first for inverse problems: the paper combines a PINN with parameter sensitivity ranking and shows exactly which bubbly-liquid parameters can be estimated to 0.8–2.1% and which one cannot be identified.

offered.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.

offered.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
offered.abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean, which machine-checks the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem. Both the interval certification and formalization were developed with substantial assistance from a large language model, while the validity of the result remains independent of the language model: the numerical bounds are rigorously enclosed by interval arithmetic and the subsequent mathematical deductions are checked by the Lean kernel. Together, these steps provide a pipeline from neural discovery to rigorous numerical certification and machine-checked verification with auditable mathematical guarantees.

offered.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
offered.abstract: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions. We examine how the learned control fields depend on the coupling, training configuration, and available local fields, including five exchange-type dipolar scenarios. We test the learned control fields under the Lindblad master equation with dephasing and amplitude damping, theoretically reproducing the expected first-order fidelity loss in the weak-dissipation regime. Finally, boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions represent 139 learned controls with a minimum common count of $K_\ast=24$ coefficients per control for all eleven family-averaged mean squared errors to fall below $10^{-6}$. Separately, square-pulse and Strang propagation at $K=30$ preserve all 31 continuous polynomial references within infidelity $10^{-5}$ at $N=128$ and all larger tested resolutions, under both sampling rules. These results connect multi-state gate synthesis, control-resource characterization, and compact square-pulse playback.

offered.title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations. Closed cell 6-plate geometries were also additively manufactured using LAPIS and experimentally characterized. The results indicate that a minimum of 6 plates is required to constitute an ultrastiff isotropic lattice, 7 plates would return the established plate Cubic Octet structure while 8 to 10 plate geometries did not show significant differences in properties. Despite the introduction of some plate bending due to sub-optimal plate placement strategy, relative stiffness of the PINNs lattices adheres closely to the Hashin Shtrikman upper bound, 90 percent of Hashin Shtrikman upper bound at a relative density of 0.4, and the lattices maintain near isotropic behaviour, achieving a Zener ratio of 0.95 at a relative density of 0.1. Benchmarking results show that specific stiffness of PINNs lattices is higher than the majority of isotropic architectures reported in the literature.

offered.title: Solving the Nonlinear Westervelt Equation in Ultrasound Propagation Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: Modeling the nonlinear acoustic wave propagation in biological tissues needs accuracy, especially in ultrasound imaging and therapeutic applications. The 1D Westervelt equation, \( p_{xx} - p_{tt} + γ\, p_{ttt} + η\,(p^{2})_{tt}=0, \) could be used to describe a finite-amplitude ultrasound propagation in these tissues. This equation accounts for nonlinearity, \(η\), and attenuation, \(γ\). To solve this equation, we observe that traditional solvers may struggle to do so correctly. This is due to the difficulties arising from the nonlinear nature of the equation. We solve the equation by defining three synthetic cases - linear (\(η=0.001\), \(γ=10^{-6}\)), shock-dominated (\(η=0.02\), \(γ=10^{-6}\)), and dissipation-dominated (\(η=0.01\), \(γ=5\times10^{-4}\)) - and using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to showcase the solution. A sinusoidal activation function is used to capture the oscillatory behavior of the problem. The results of our study, with PDE residual converging to at least \(10^{-6}\), boundary condition loss to \(10^{-5}\), and the PINN loss converging to \(10^{-5}\) for each case at \(30,000\) epochs, show that \(γ\) scales the rate of amplitude decay, while \(η\) governs frequency-dependent phase speeds.

offered.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
offered.abstract: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function $ρ$, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant $c$: linear diffusion ($c=-1$, $ω\equiv0$), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap ($c=-1$, $ω\neq0$), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency ($c=+1$). An exact moment identity gives $ρ$ in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is comparative: each family requires a different component of the construction and has a different honest control. In family I, the diffusive-time reparametrisation alone reproduces most of the gain, so that family is a poor test of the idea and shows why an ablation is mandatory. In family II no time reparametrisation exists, the control degrades accuracy, and the amplitude prefactor becomes essential (40.8x). In family III the adiabatic approximation also fails, and the quadratic phase factor is what matters (5.7x). The method does not help when the reduced solution does not converge to a fixed point: its extrapolation advantage then disappears. The reduction itself is the classical scaling-variable change of the self-similar-asymptotics literature; what is new is the moment identity that makes it architectural for time-dependent coefficients, and the comparative anatomy above.

offered.title: A Physics Informed Neural Network Approach to Decipher Environmental Confinement of Molecular Clouds in the Third Galactic Quadrant
offered.abstract: Recent high-sensitivity and high-resolution surveys of the Third Galactic Quadrant [$219.75 \leq l \leq 229.75$ and $-5.25 \leq b \leq 5.25$], such as the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting ( MWISP) survey, have revealed a significant population of molecular clouds (MCs) that appear virially unbound ($α_{vir} > 2$) according to traditional isolated MC models. However, these apparently unstable cloud structures are actually found long-lived and actively undertaking star formation. This inconsistency presents a Virial Paradox. In the present work, we employ a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to address this discrepancy by re-evaluating the stability of 2,091 MCs . Unlike traditional machine learning, our PINN model embeds the complete Eulerian Virial Theorem including external surface pressure support ($P_{ext}$) directly into the network's loss function. This model autonomously discovers a global Galactic pressure field that scales inversely with vertical height ($|z|$) and Galactocentric radius ($R_{GC}$), consistent with the properties of the Galactic Flare. By incorporating this AI-derived pressure support, we demonstrate a dramatic shift in the stability census: 99.9\% of previously thought unbound clouds are found to be in a state of pressure confined equilibrium ($α_{AI} \leq 2$). Furthermore, we find a robust log-log correlation ($R = 0.64$) between our corrected stability parameter and the star formation rate (SFR). This correlation provides independent physical validation that environmental confinement is a primary regulator of star forming efficiency in the outer Galaxy.

offered.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
offered.abstract: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

offered.title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
offered.abstract: We develop a physics-informed method for aerodynamic shape optimisation of turbine blades, treating the flow field and blade geometry as coupled unknowns. The method translates prescribed surface-pressure distributions into geometric modifications through pressure-target continuation and alternating flow-geometry updates. A differentiable representation of the blade surfaces allows their positions and orientations to be optimised within the current flow field, followed by flow re-adaptation to the modified boundaries. The inverse formulation uses the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations as physics constraints and is evaluated on the LS89 turbine cascade using 28 pressure-target points derived from experimental data. Starting from a modified profile and a warm-started flow network, the final pressure-side and suction-side root-mean-square fitting errors are 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure, respectively. Independent forward verification with SharC reproduces the principal surface-pressure trends of the experimental measurements, with remaining differences near the trailing edge. These results demonstrate the translation of experimental-origin loading data into geometric blade modifications through coordinated optimisation of the flow field and moving boundaries.

offered.title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
offered.abstract: In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.

offered.title: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN)
offered.abstract: We present a variational functional neural network (vfNN) algorithm that optimizes physically motivated continuum functionals in integral form (e.g., Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy) to find the states of a system. That way, vfNN bypasses solving the equations of motion (a.k.a. the Euler-Lagrange equations), which are in the form of differential equations. To this end, our approach is fundamentally different from conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINN) that solve differential equations by minimizing a phenomenological loss function involving higher order derivatives and ad hoc weight factors. In contrast, vfNN merely evaluates lower order derivatives of the generating functional and replaces the weight factors with rigorous physical scales. This also fundamentally changes the loss landscape, and the desired solutions may become unstable. For this emergent nonconvex optimization problem, we develop a quasi-Newton optimization algorithm with simulated annealing that converges to the solutions of the corresponding Euler-Lagrange equations of the functional regardless of their stability properties. Our simulations using vfNN give accurate results for benchmark systems governed by linear or nonlinear ordinary differential equations.

offered.title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks(PINNs) offer a mesh-free and continuously differentiable approach to fluid simulation. However, standard monolithic PINNs for incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations often suffer from severe constraint coupling and spectral biases, limiting both convergence and accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a segregated, iterative, and multi-stage PINN (SIM-PINN) inspired by the classical projection method in computational fluid dynamics. In SIM-PINN, the nonlinear NS equations are decoupled into the linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations. Each is addressed separately using dedicated multi-stage neural networks and coupled through projection-based inner iterations. Each stage of the multi-stage neural networks for the momentum equations corresponds to one iteration of the projection method, in which the velocity fields are progressively refined at targeted frequencies. Upon iteration convergence, solutions to the fully coupled and nonlinear NS equations are recovered. By integrating the segregated and iterative framework with the multi-stage training, SIM-PINN alleviates the optimization difficulties of the incompressible NS equations arising from nonlinearity, constraint coupling, and spectral biases. The improved convergence and accuracy are demonstrated by simulations of steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flows.

offered.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
offered.abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

offered.title: Adaptive Domain Decomposition for Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: In this work, we present adaptive domain decomposition finite basis physics-informed neural networks (ADD-FBPINNs). The proposed method integrates Partition of Unity Networks (POUNets), a data-driven approach for learning domain partitions, with finite Basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs) to perform more efficient domain decomposition and achieve more accurate approximations. FBPINNs improve upon the accuracy of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) through user-defined subdivisions of the computational domain. By adapting the domain decomposition based on the solution's features using a separable POUNet, the framework can automatically learn partitions that are stable and can be geometrically interpretable. We test this approach on the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation, two-dimensional Poisson equation with multiscale features, and viscous Burgers equation and observe improved accuracy compared with FBPINNs with fixed domain decomposition.

offered.title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
offered.abstract: Physics informed machine learning provides a framework to study and simulate fluid dynamics, potentially at a fraction of the computational cost of traditional numerical methods, with the goal of improving the explainability, accuracy and robustness of purely data driven machine learning methods. In this work, we extend the hard constraint projection (HCP) method developed by Chen et al. [Journal of Computational Physics, 445, 110624, 2021] from a linear partial differential equation (PDE) to a nonlinear PDE: the 1D Burgers' equation. To strictly impose a discrete approximation of the governing equation, the Burgers' equation is first locally discretised (using a finite difference stencil) then decomposed into a constraint matrix and a prediction matrix. Using tools from linear algebra, the constraint matrix is used to construct a projection matrix. A physics informed neural network (PINN) [Raissi et al. Journal of Computational Physics, 378, 686, 2019] is used to predict the velocity, and a final unlearnable layer projects the velocity prediction to the hyperplane of exact solutions to a discretised form of the Burgers' equation. Our initial results indicate that the HCP-PINN initially trains similarly to an equivalent PINN, and as the PINN loss plateaus, the HCP-PINN loss continues to decline. When tested on a previously unseen uniform grid of points covering the domain, the HCP-PINN exhibits higher accuracy, converging to a data error approximately an order of magnitude lower than the comparable PINN. We also observe that the inclusion of the HCP layer results in better observance of the governing PDE. Our findings suggest that the HCP-PINN can be more robust to the selection of physics collocation points, and less dependent on collocation point quantity.

offered.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
offered.abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

offered.title: Equation informed time reparametrization for physics informed neural networks
offered.abstract: Physics Informed Neural Networks offer a mesh-free approach to solving differential equations, but their application to time-dependent problems remains challenging, particularly when the governing dynamics involve widely different time scales. With collocation points spread uniformly in time, short intervals of rapid change are under resolved. This work introduces an equation informed time reparameterization framework that modifies the temporal coordinate used during PINN training based on the local dynamics of the governing equation. The proposed method follows a two stage procedure. First, a pilot PINN training provides an approximate solution, which is used to linearize the governing differential operator and estimate its local response to small perturbations. These responses are combined into a time-dependent rate function, large where the dynamics are fast, that defines a strictly increasing transformation from physical time to a new computational time coordinate. A second PINN is then trained on the transformed governing equation, with uniformly sampled collocation points in the new coordinate producing a nonuniform distribution in physical time. Different combination rules and spatial reduction strategies are considered. With the cost of the pilot training included, the method reduces the error by a factor of 4 to 29 relative to the best alternative method on the Kachanov Rabotnov creep-damage model near rupture, and by a factor of 5 to 16 relative to every alternative method on the Frank-Kamenetskii equation near blow up.

offered.title: A Two-Dimensional Physics-Informed Neural Network Model of a Hall Effect Thruster Plasma: Self-Consistent Electrostatics and Physical-Consistency Diagnostics
offered.abstract: We present a two-dimensional axisymmetric physics-informed neural network (PINN) of the discharge channel of the P5 Hall thruster at 300 V and 5.4 A, which solves eleven coupled plasma fields and assimilates 145 internal probe measurements per field reconstructed from the data of Haas and Gallimore. The electric potential is obtained from Poisson's equation in charge-separation form, n_e = n_i(1+eta), with eta bounded by construction, which keeps the stiff electrostatic constraint active and trainable. The reference solution agrees with the training profiles to relative L2 errors of 0.017, 0.073 and 0.205 for the potential, electron temperature and ion density, and held-out tests show the potential to be far more robust than the ion density to the withdrawal of measurement lines. We then test the solution against requirements the data fit does not reveal: global particle and current balances, the electron current implied by the momentum equation, the field-aligned electron force balance and the axial ion momentum budget. These expose a neutral inflow six times the measured flow, a bound in the potential representation, and a momentum-implied electron current, more than 99% field-aligned, exceeding the discharge current by orders of magnitude. Correcting these, with a divergence-free magnetic field fitted to measured data, uncertainty-weighted data, the electron pressure gradient and progressively imposed field-aligned and current constraints, yields a solution that conserves particles to within 3%, holds the current between 5.1 and 5.4 A and places 97% of the potential and 88% of the temperature measurements within their uncertainties. Within the tested single-velocity fluid formulation, however, the ion density, potential and ion velocity could not be matched together, and the field-aligned electron balance remains the main obstacle to electron self-consistency.

offered.title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
offered.abstract: Existing models of social media virality either prescribe the functional form of engagement growth or assume a fixed mechanism by which past activity influences future engagement. We present a fractional physics-informed neural network that learns both the temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of social media engagement, using symbolic regression to translate the learned dynamics into interpretable equations. Synthetic experiments at the deployment resolution of 24 hourly observations demonstrate that the fractional order and reaction law can be jointly recovered from clean data. Under observation noise, however, the standard pointwise physics residual drives the fractional order toward its lower bound through a scale artifact. We address this failure using a fully whitened residual that propagates observation noise through the fractional operator. Applying the framework to 348 posts from X (formerly Twitter), we find that a single-window model estimates strongly memory-dependent dynamics but fails to accurately reconstruct held-out trajectories. Partitioning the 24-hour window into four teacher-forced segments substantially improves performance, yielding segment-specific fractional orders that increase from 0.23 to 0.99 and interpretable growth laws for each phase. The segmented model reconstructs 64% of held-out trajectories within a mean squared error of 0.01, compared with 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of fractional physics-informed equation discovery to uncover interpretable engagement dynamics while highlighting the importance of noise-aware estimation and temporal segmentation.

offered.title: A sensor-driven physics-informed neural network for real-time occupant-centric space heating control
offered.abstract: Conventional space heating systems typically rely on single or sparse fixed-point temperature measurements, overlooking non-uniform indoor temperature distributions, transient thermal dynamics, and occupant-specific comfort requirements. This study explores an occupant-centric control strategy that aims to maintain the desired temperature around the occupant location. Spatially and temporally varying temperature fields, together with occupant mobility, make real-time local temperature estimation challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a control-oriented Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model for indoor temperature-field prediction. Conventional PINNs rely on explicit time inputs and assume consistent temporal patterns across samples, which limits adaptability under variable initial conditions and heating sequences. The proposed model infers temporal dynamics implicitly from spatial coordinates and limited sensor measurements, improving robustness to changes in initial conditions and external disturbances. The method was validated across nine horizontal sensing planes in three controlled room-scale configurations. Against a validated COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, the PINN predicted the evaluated temperature fields with a maximum relative error below 1.85% across validation cases. These predictions supported an occupant-centric space heating control scheme. Compared with COMSOL-based offline control, the PINN-based system achieved an average prediction error of around 0.67%, and its rapid inference supports real-time occupant-centric control implementation. This work represents a move away from reliance on fixed-point temperature measurements in space heating control to an occupant-centric control strategy informed by real-time environmental feedback.

overviews.overview: This period’s PINN work pushed into harder inverse and nonlinear regimes while tightening numerical guarantees. In black-hole perturbation theory, a PINN with exact horizon conditions and an H2-Sobolev residual loss recovered scalar, vector, and tensor Love numbers with relative errors below 10^-5, and the higher-derivative terms improved accuracy by orders of magnitude [2611.02084]. On nonlinear water waves, PINNs were used as a search engine for periodic gravity-capillary traveling waves, reaching near-machine-precision residuals and enabling rigorous interval-arithmetic certification plus Lean formalization of a candidate solution [2611.07395]. Other papers leaned on structure-preserving constraints: exact boundary/initial embeddings cut e15 identification errors to 0.15%–0.51% [2611.03485], and a projection-style segregated PINN improved incompressible Navier-Stokes convergence by decoupling momentum and pressure [2611.07387].

picks.hook: Best starting point if you care about what PINNs can do when paired with certification: it shows near-machine-precision nonlinear wave solving, then independently bounds the residual with interval arithmetic and formalizes the proof in Lean.

A clean benchmark for high-accuracy PINNs on a controlled GR problem: exact horizon enforcement plus an H2-Sobolev loss gets Love numbers to below 10^-5 relative error and isolates solver error from response-extraction error.

offered.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme. Moreover, the studies set the surrounding and not considered components of the pipeline to a minimal default that is no longer representative of current best practice approaches. Conclusions drawn under such conditions may not transfer to competitive pipelines. In this work, we propose a new evaluation protocol that (1) treats the four components as an integrated system; (2) crucially requires competitive implementations of the components not under investigation; (3) specifies the metrics and reporting format; and (4) is accompanied by structured documentation that ensures the traceability of evaluations across studies. Based on this comprehensive protocol, we release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems. Using PINNpipe, we illustrate our evaluation protocol in relation to established benchmark studies and report results that challenge common assumptions.

offered.title: Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. The residual is a weak space--time control-volume identity enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap, so no mesh is needed. In free-surface variables, the geometric source is integrated by parts onto the bed, so that the network is never differentiated, and a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities, located from the bathymetry alone, separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head. We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family, quadrature order and nominal bed slope, so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective; that the continuous residual characterises weak solutions; that the slope correction is consistent; and that no approximation with a continuous free surface can satisfy the head condition at a step with non-zero discharge, so that the decomposition is necessary. Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off on four lake-at-rest configurations over smooth, discontinuous, compound and tabulated beds, and the trained network reaches the equilibrium to round-off under an extended training budget. On seven Riemann problems at a bottom step, covering sub-, super- and critical transitions, the network attains relative $L^1$ free-surface errors between $6.9\times10^{-4}$ and $3.5\times10^{-3}$, and reaches critical states without prescribing them.

offered.title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{α,p}(0,T;L^2(Ω))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.

offered.title: Modal-Augmented Chebyshev Physics-Informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Power Systems
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a promising alternative to numerical integration for power system dynamic simulation; however, their conventional architectures can struggle to capture electromechanical oscillations. Although physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (PIKANs) offer an alternative, their B-spline implementations incur substantial training costs. To address these limitations, this paper investigates Chebyshev PIKANs (c-PIKANs) and proposes a modal-augmented c-PIKAN (mac-PIKAN) based on a trial solution that incorporates the closed-form modal response of the linearized swing equation. First, the modal response is used to capture the dominant oscillatory dynamics. Then, a c-PIKAN learns a nonlinear correction weighted by a quadratic time-dependent factor, ensuring that the initial rotor angle and speed are satisfied exactly. Evaluations on the single-machine infinite-bus benchmark demonstrate the computational efficiency of c-PIKAN and show that mac-PIKAN reduces PINN rotor-angle and frequency errors from 1.59% to 0.29% and from 5.26% to 0.99%, respectively, while maintaining higher accuracy across training-data sizes and at lower damping levels.

offered.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
offered.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. Experiments on four PDEs, namely the heat, advection, Burgers', and Allen--Cahn equations, demonstrate lower solution errors than conventional physics-informed neural networks, while revealing limitations in satisfying the governing equations for nonlinear PDEs.

offered.title: Residual-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Network KKL Observers with Input-to-State Stability Guarantees
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) Kazantzis--Kravaris--Luenberger (KKL) observers require an approximate solution to a KKL partial differential equation (PDE) and an approximate inverse of this solution. Either approximation can leave a nonzero estimation bias even without measurement noise. In this paper, we remove both errors from the implemented observer by construction. We build an encoder containing an explicitly invertible neural map. Its closed-form inverse provides the internal state reconstruction used to evaluate the learned KKL residual and correct the latent dynamics. This construction makes the synchronization manifold exactly invariant for every value of the network weights. Based on contraction of the residual-corrected observer dynamics, we prove an input-to-state stability (ISS) result for the implemented error dynamics with respect to measurement noise. A direct consequence is that the estimation error converges exponentially to zero in the noise-free setting. We provide two numerical examples, the Van der Pol oscillator and the chaotic Lorenz system, in which the residual-corrected observers achieve exact noise-free convergence and improved error responses compared with released PINN--KKL baselines.

offered.title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
offered.abstract: Embedded microfluidic cooling is a promising technology for dissipating the intense heat generated by high-performance electronic chips. However, the design and optimization of such coolers impose prohibitive computational costs when using conventional numerical solvers. Here, we present a parameterized physics-informed neural network (PINN) as a deep learning framework for rapidly and accurately predicting the thermohydraulic performance of embedded manifold microchannels. By incorporating four geometric dimensions along with three spatial coordinates as the network inputs, the proposed model enables multiphysics prediction across a continuous design space. Remarkably, our predicted velocity and temperature fields differ from finite-element simulations by relative errors of only 8.1% and 5.6%, respectively, while reducing the computational time and cost by over four orders of magnitude. Key to this framework is a composite strategy combining geometric ansatz embedding, the SOAP optimizer, and a thermal-conductivity-based curriculum learning scheme, which helps overcome the convergence challenges inherent in training PINNs for complex three-dimensional flows. Notably, by leveraging a highly optimized JAX backend, the network achieves convergence on a single consumer-grade GPU in less than four hours. Our approach offers a physics-consistent, real-time surrogate model that can substantially accelerate innovations in advanced microfluidic cooling of future electronics.

offered.title: Beyond Accuracy: Physics-Informed Evaluation of ANN-based Power Flow Solvers under System Shift
offered.abstract: Recent advances in artificial deep learning-based power flow (PF) solvers have primarily focused on improving estimation accuracy, while their physical feasibility and operational reliability under realistic system variations remain insufficiently evaluated. This paper proposes a physics-informed evaluation framework for deep learning-based PF solvers under topology and load distribution shifts. Beyond conventional voltage-domain errors, the framework incorporates KCL gaps, branch-flow gaps, KVL residuals, continuous feasibility scores, and strict, practical, and relaxed PF feasibility rates. Four case studies are designed to investigate topology shifts, mixed topology training, load distribution shifts, and combined topology distribution shifts. Eight ANN architectures, including graph input models, load-only baselines, and physics-informed neural networks, are evaluated under consistent settings. The results demonstrate that low estimation errors do not necessarily correspond to physically feasible or operationally reliable PF solutions, particularly under combined system shifts. The proposed framework establishes an initial foundation and analysis for the development and verification of trustworthy deep learning-based PF solvers, providing support for their reliable deployment in future AI-enabled power system analysis.

offered.title: A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
offered.abstract: Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.

offered.title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime $(1-β_2)/(1-β_1)\ll1$. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ($Re=100,400$) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.

offered.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
offered.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

offered.title: Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
offered.abstract: We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic Hölder space \(C^{2+α,1+α/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.

offered.title: PINNverse meets Jordan--Wigner: learning the Hamiltonian of long spin chains
offered.abstract: Inverse physics-informed neural networks (PINNverse) learn the parameters of a quantum Hamiltonian from measured expectation values, but the network output grows as $4^N$ with the number of qubits $N$. We show that, for spin chains with nearest-neighbor exchange interactions, the Jordan-Wigner transformation removes this exponential cost: the dynamics closes on an $N\times N$ one-body density matrix, so the network needs only $N^2$ outputs and the data are local observables measured in five global settings. Parasitic $ZZ$ couplings (crosstalk) are included through a time-dependent Hartree--Fock closure. With synthetic data, the same network first solves the equation of motion and then recovers the Hamiltonian parameters of chains of up to $50$ qubits, with couplings learned to better than $0.1\%$. Errors in the local frequencies of long chains are removed by a direct least-squares fit started from the network estimate.

offered.title: Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach
offered.abstract: In this work, we develop an efficient Gauss-Newton optimization approach for finite basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs). The key ingredient is the overlapping domain decomposition architecture of FBPINNs, which localizes the influence of each subnetwork and induces block sparsity in both the residual Jacobian and the corresponding Gauss-Newton matrix. We characterize this structure and exploit it through sparse automatic differentiation, using graph coloring to partition structurally orthogonal Jacobian columns or rows. This reduces differentiation costs and memory requirements while preserving all structurally nonzero derivative information. The resulting compressed Jacobian representations allow us to assemble the Gauss-Newton system directly in block-sparse form, enabling the use of sparse direct solvers and preconditioned iterative methods. In this way, the otherwise expensive second-order optimization problem is reduced to scalable sparse linear algebra. We demonstrate the approach on multiscale PDEs, where accurate approximation requires rich neural network parametrizations and large numbers of collocation points. Numerical experiments show that our block-sparse Gauss-Newton method attains high accuracy and substantially accelerates optimization relative to first-order baselines while remaining computationally tractable for large problem sizes.

offered.title: Data-Driven Conservation Laws for Newtonian Systems: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Eisenhart-Duval Geometry
offered.abstract: We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network approach for the data-driven reconstruction of the symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamical systems, based on the geometrization of the dynamics through the Eisenhart-Duval lift. Within the Eisenhart-Duval lift, the symmetry conditions reduce to the linear Killing or Conformal Killing equations of the extended metric. We combine a Hamiltonian neural network, which reconstructs the potential function from the data, with a random-feature neural network, which solves the symmetry conditions for the collineations of the extended geometry. From the learned vector fields we construct the Lie algebra and, through Noether's theorem, the corresponding conserved quantities, while the derivation of the curvature invariants for the extended geometry provide allow us to perform an independent consistency test. We apply the method to the one-dimensional Ermakov-Pinney equation and to the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, with and without a quartic perturbation, by using different level of noise in the phase-space data. For the Ermakov-Pinney equation, the three Killing vectors of the flat extended plane, and the corresponding nonlocal conservation laws, are recovered for, while for the harmonic oscillator, the ten conformal Killing vectors which form the $so(3,2)$ Lie algebra are determined for noise levels up to $10\%$. When the quartic term is added, the broken symmetries are identified as approximate symmetries.

offered.title: A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
offered.abstract: Optimal allocation of generators is a key challenge in power systems to achieve economical dispatch while satisfying operational constraints. Conventional optimization techniques can be computationally expensive, limiting their applicability in real-time environments, and neural networks often require offline retraining under new operating conditions. This paper proposes a three-stage unsupervised online physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for optimal power flow (OPF). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework satisfies load demand and system constraints while achieving a $43,665 lower operating cost than fmincon-based optimization under the same operating conditions. The training process analysis further demonstrate the framework's ability to adapt its parameters online to variations in load demand and renewable generation in real time.

offered.title: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
offered.abstract: The Adam optimizer is widely used to train neural networks with highly nonlinear and nonconvex objective functions. Remarkably, Adam often drives the empirical training loss nearly to zero. This phenomenon has been partially explained by neural tangent kernel (NTK) analyses of gradient descent (GD) and stochastic gradient descent (SGD). However, analyzing Adam presents additional challenges. Its first-moment momentum couples stochastic gradients across iterations, while its adaptive second-moment preconditioner depends on the same stochastic gradient used in the update. In this paper, we establish linear convergence guarantees for Adam in training sufficiently wide two-layer neural networks with either full-batch or minibatch gradients. For full-batch Adam, we construct a Lyapunov function to control the effect of historical momentum. For minibatch Adam, our analysis builds on an exact virtual-iterate representation, a conditional analysis of the dependence between stochastic gradients and adaptive preconditioners, and uniform concentration bounds for the second-moment estimates. We prove geometric decay of the empirical loss for full-batch Adam and geometric decay in restricted expectation on a high-probability event for minibatch Adam. Beyond regression, we extend our convergence analysis to physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for solving the Poisson equation, where differential operators and separate sampling of interior and boundary points introduce additional challenges. We establish analogous global convergence guarantees for both deterministic and stochastic Adam under explicit conditions on network width and Adam's parameters, characterizing the effects of minibatch size on convergence. These results help bridge the gap between Adam's empirical success and its theoretical understanding, providing sharper convergence guarantees for PINNs than existing analyses.

offered.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
offered.abstract: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses. Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.

offered.title: Media Trading with Censored Auction Prices: A Stochastic Control and Reinforcement Learning Approach
offered.abstract: In real-time bidding, marketing agencies must balance campaign performance, transaction margins and the use of a finite advertising budget. A key difficulty is that market-clearing prices are typically observed only when bids are successful, so the information available for subsequent decisions depends on the bidding policy. We formulate this problem using a continuous-time stochastic control model with a latent price process. To construct a price signal, we consider parallel exploratory subcampaigns in which bids are randomized subject to an upper bound. Under a stylized cross-sectional sampling model, the resulting price estimator is consistent and satisfies a mean-square error bound of order $N^{-1}$, where $N$ is the number of exploratory observations. We then describe a model-based approach combining forward-equation calibration with Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman policy iteration and a physics-informed neural network, alongside an entropy-regularized actor-critic approach based on observable information in a model-free setting. Synthetic experiments illustrate the estimator and the computational procedures. The framework clarifies the decision and information trade-offs faced by the agency, while distinguishing full-information benchmarks and estimated-price policies from the genuinely partially observed control problem.

overviews.overview: This period splits between making PINNs more trustworthy as a research tool and making them more faithful to PDE structure. PINNeval argues that many benchmark claims are fragile because they isolate one pipeline component while freezing the rest at noncompetitive defaults; it instead evaluates domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, architecture, and optimization as an integrated system, and ships PINNpipe with 18 methods and nine benchmark problems [2611.08559]. On the modeling side, a weak/entropy PINN is extended to shallow water with smooth and discontinuous bathymetry, using randomly placed overlapping control volumes, exact bed-slope correction, and subdomain coupling so the lake-at-rest residual vanishes to round-off and is an exact global minimizer [2611.17289].

picks.hook: Start here for the evaluation protocol: it formalizes what a fair PINN benchmark should hold fixed, what must be competitive, and provides PINNpipe with 18 methods and nine problems.

Best read for structure-preserving PINNs: it proves exact lake-at-rest minimization over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry and shows how weak residuals, bed corrections, and subdomain coupling fit together.

offered.title: Solving Linear Systems in $\widetilde{O}(mn \log \fracκε)$ Bit Operations
offered.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm that solves a nonsingular linear system $Ax=b$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ has $m$ nonzero entries and condition number $κ$, to any relative residual tolerance $0<ε\le1/2$ using $\widetilde{O(}mn\log(κ/ε))$ bit operations for inputs with logarithmically many bits per entry. For sparse, polynomially conditioned systems with $m=\widetilde{O}(n)$, this gives an $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ algorithm for any inverse-polynomial accuracy, improving on the algorithm of Peng and Vempala, as sharpened by Nie, whose running time in this regime is approximately $O(n^{2.2707})$ with the best current matrix multiplication exponent, and largely closing a gap between the idealized performance of the conjugate gradient method in exact arithmetic and the running time achievable with finite-precision computation that has persisted for over 70 years. The algorithm is surprisingly simple. For integer inputs, we apply Dixon's lifting algorithm to the perturbed system $(A+I/R)x=b$ for a suitable integer $R$. After scaling, the matrix of this system is $RA+I\equiv I\pmod R$, so its modular inverse is trivial, and each lifting step needs only a sparse matrix-vector product with $A$ on $O(\log R)$-bit numbers. Fast rational reconstruction then recovers the exact solution of the perturbed system, which is an $ε$-accurate solution of the original one. Normalization and rounding extend the result to fixed-point and floating-point inputs, with floating-point outputs represented using short integer significands and a common encoded exponent. A computable certificate removes the need for prior knowledge of $κ$.

offered.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
offered.abstract: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $ΔV(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{NΔV(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we compare it with exact stochastic simulation of population-threshold crossing times regressed in $N$. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $ΔV(r)=ΔV_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $ΔV_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first. At $r=1$, the barrier is 55% larger than $ΔV_\infty$. The saddle barrier $ΔV(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, but the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply: at $r=0.5$ the cheapest crossing costs 7.7% less action, keeps the signal high, and is usually followed by recovery. Simulated arrival times in this neighbourhood, which include failed attempts, grow with slopes within two fitted standard errors of the saddle barrier at every tested rate, and within $0.004$ of it if the logarithmic prefactor term is omitted. Under either regression model they exclude $ΔV_\infty$ at $r\le2$ by at least $4.4$ fitted standard errors, without using the action solver.

offered.title: Addressing Data Engineering Challenges in the Cold-Chain Sector to Reduce its Environmental Impact Through Analytics
offered.abstract: Data analytics offer a great opportunity for organizations within the cold-chain industry to become more sustainable and reduce their environmental footprint. Yet, despite recent progress in data sciences, they still face challenges to ensure data quality and streamline data processes through adapted full-scale ecosystems, limiting their ability to perform sustainable analytics. Most data techniques and tools stem from the data-science community and are not always suitably adapted to domain specificities. For instance, nearly all data-quality frameworks are designed to individually consider entities, i.e. representations of real-world elements. However, achieving environmental impact reduction in industrial settings, particularly within the cold-chain sector, often requires modelling and studying entire systems comprised of multiple interdependent entities. This publication challenges the application of conventional data science and engineering concepts in data ecosystems within the cold-chain sector and proposes an alternative approach to sustainably address prevalent challenges and thus optimize analytical processes.

offered.title: Broken Symmetry in BF16 Attention: Why FlashAttention Gradients Blow Up Late in Training
offered.abstract: BF16 is now standard in large-scale pretraining, including in fused attention kernels such as FlashAttention, and these kernels are widely trusted. When we used FlashAttention-3 to pretrain a 450M-parameter transformer on 50B tokens, however, we ran into a problem: training was healthy for 25B tokens, then the gradient norm grew a thousandfold and the loss ended 0.2 nats above FP32 attention, without a single NaN. Recomputing the attention backward of just two layers in FP32 removes almost all of the excess gradient. Part of the cause is known: a fused multiply-add in the forward softmax, so far treated as an extreme-input NaN case and never fixed in FlashAttention-3. Repairing it stops the blow-up, but the query gradient is still wrong by more than its own size, and training still drives attention logits to thousands of times their size under accurate gradients. The remaining error comes from a broken conservation law. The softmax score gradient sums to zero along every row, which makes the query gradient blind to where the keys sit as a group; rounding it to BF16 leaves a small nonzero sum that leaks the mean key into the gradient, and the leak grows exactly as late training makes keys large and attention sharp. We introduce GProj (gauge projection), which restores the zero sum after the cast with two rank-one corrections per row. It cuts the remaining median query/key gradient errors from 219%/13% to 0.34%/0.37%, on par with FP32 attention, for 4.7% more time per training step. In matched from-scratch runs it trains to the same loss as FP32 attention, while FlashAttention-3 and key smoothing both destabilize.

offered.title: Spectral analysis of a class of IRK stage preconditioners for linear wave equations
offered.abstract: We lay out the analysis of the ``Kronecker preconditioners'' adopted in [24] for the linear wave equations. Importantly, we deliver the analysis justifying the claims in~[24, Section 4.2] about these preconditioners and we unpack all of the necessary numerical background for a full understanding of the observed phenomena.

offered.title: Universal Approximation of Measure-to-Measure Operators by Pushforwards
offered.abstract: Many learning tasks map an input distribution to an output distribution. A natural way to model such an operator is to transform each input sample using a continuous function that may depend on the entire input distribution, and then take the distribution of the transformed samples. This defines a measure-dependent pushforward model and includes measure-theoretic formulations of transformers. We ask when such models can approximate arbitrary continuous operators between spaces of probability measures. We first show that universal approximation fails when atomic inputs are allowed: some continuous measure-to-measure operators that split or redistribute atomic mass cannot be approximated arbitrarily well by deterministic pushforward models. We then introduce the uniform level set condition, which requires a continuous measure-dependent scalarization whose shrinking level set neighborhoods carry uniformly vanishing mass over the input family. This condition is satisfied, in particular, by compact families of absolutely continuous measures. On every compact family satisfying this condition, we prove that any continuous measure-to-measure operator with outputs of finite $p$-th moment can be uniformly approximated, in the $p$-Wasserstein distance, by continuous measure-dependent pushforwards. Combining our theorem with existing approximation results for measure-dependent in-context maps yields universal approximation by measure-theoretic transformers.
