Tropical roots guide the construction, and their multiplicities reduce the number of required solves. These results provide a basis for coefficientwise relative backward stability across the spectrum.

offered.title: Fast and Stable Arbitrary Precision Approximate Matrix Multiplication
offered.abstract: We present several new and surprising results on the theory and practice of Arbitrary Precision Approximate (APA) matrix multiplication, which refers to algorithms that output merely approximations to matrix multiplication even in exact arithmetic. While APA algorithms have been around for nearly half a century, and despite the fact that they have potentially lower (asymptotic) cost than many fast exact matrix multiplication schemes, they have not been studied as closely, to the extent that relatively little is known about their numerical properties. In this paper, we shine a spotlight on these algorithms by presenting three important results. First, we provide a new search algorithm for APA routines that is easy to use, automatically generates encoding matrices with functional entries, and can match or beat the best known APA algorithms for several sizes. In particular, we improve the upper bound on the border rank of $\langle 2,4,5 \rangle$ matrix multiplication. Second, we combine this insight with alternative bases to minimize the number of additions in an APA algorithm, thereby improving its leading coefficient. Finally, we prove the same kind of stability that characterizes fast exact matrix multiplication for an algorithm of Bini [Calcolo 1980] that computes an exact product of two matrices using a modified APA scheme (with or without alternative bases).

offered.title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
offered.abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

offered.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
offered.abstract:
We approximate the solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$ of $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$ by operator networks whose only primitives are heat-semigroup functions of a fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The main result is an emulation theorem on strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Émery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$: an explicit scheme reaches $\dot H^1$-error $\varepsilon$ uniformly over coefficients with bounded carré du champ and bounded generator image and over $L^2$ data, with parameters depending only on the coefficient bounds, the accuracy and $K$; on the torus this gives a $C^2$-type coefficient class with constants independent of the dimension. The torus version refines this to Wiener classes of fractional regularity $A^{1+θ}$, with an explicit rate attained by the scheme's product-defect block. The scheme unrolls the Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, controls each inexact step in the operator norm of $\dot H^1$ without Galerkin truncation, and synthesises the coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$ from the product defect of one heat layer. All parameters are explicit; the results are approximation theorems for continuum operators.

offered.title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
offered.abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $Φ(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{Φ,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.

offered.title: C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
offered.abstract: This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.

offered.title: Least-Squares Finite Element Methods with Weakly Imposed Boundary Conditions: Norm and Error Equivalences, Over-Penalization, and Fully Discontinuous Discretizations
offered.abstract: Weakly imposed boundary conditions in first-order system least-squares methods go back to Jespersen (1977), but two questions have remained open for decades: the right weights, especially for the Neumann residual, whose natural norm $H^{-1/2}$ suggests $h_F$, and norm and error equivalences, especially for indefinite equations. We answer both for general, possibly indefinite, second-order elliptic equations with non-homogeneous mixed boundary conditions. First, for the weights $h_F^{-1}$ on the Dirichlet and $1$ on the Neumann residual, we prove norm and error equivalences with mesh-independent constants for every discrete pair: the error in a mesh-dependent norm is equivalent to the square root of the functional plus a Dirichlet data term. The least-squares solution converges optimally in $H(\mathrm{div};Ω)\times H^{1}(Ω)$, and the functional is a reliable and efficient error estimator, with a recovered flux also for approximations from other methods, even ones violating the boundary conditions. The key idea is to apply the stability of the boundary value problem to pairs that are discrete only in their Dirichlet traces, whose $H^{1/2}$ norm an inverse inequality bounds by the weighted penalty. Second, these weights are the right ones: weaker powers, including $h_F$ on the Neumann boundary, destroy the norm equivalence, and stronger weights are admissible, since the penalty multiplies zero at a comparison function meeting the projected data. Third, for the fully discontinuous counterpart, a pure penalty method with both jumps weighted by $h_F^{-1}$, the error equivalence holds for every discrete pair, also for exact fluxes with normal traces not square integrable on interior faces.

offered.title: Numerical Smoothness and Error Analysis for Evolution Equations
offered.abstract: This is a lecture note to introduce the innovative concept of numerical smoothness and its application in the error analysis of numerical solutions of evolution equations. We start from the two fundamentally different error splittings. One splitting is popular, which brings us to local error defined along the original solution and error propagation by numerical schemes. The well know Lax Equivalence Theorem is based on this error splitting. The other splitting can only be seen in a few numerical ODE books, which brings us to local error defined along the numerical solution and error propagation by the solutions of the evolution equations. The innovative concept of numerical smoothness arises from the second error splitting. While there are many difficulties when we use numerical stability in error analysis of nonlinear evolution equations, we will show that numerical smoothness works naturally in error analysis/estimation/control with advantages in several ways. We will define temporal and spatial numerical smoothness indicators, prove the necessity of the boundedness of these indicators for having optimal convergence rate, and show computable error estimates as functions of these smoothness indicators. Moreover, these error estimates are optimal in the approximatons' convergence rates and also optimal in the error propagation of the evolution equation. In comparison with error analysis framework of the Lax Equivalence Theorem, from the necessity results and the error estimates proven in the numerical smoothness framework, we have a new equivalence theory: Consistency + Numerical Smoothness <=> optimal error estimates. Unlike the Lax Equivalence Theorem, the new equivalence theory works well for nonlinear problems, nonlinear schemes, and many other complications of problems.

offered.title: Energy conserving compatible space--time FEM for deterministic and stochastic rotating shallow water
offered.abstract: We present a fully discrete energy conserving discretisation of the rotating shallow water equations with arbitrary order in space and time. A space time finite element discretisation is used, built from compatible finite element methods in space and continuous Petrov-Galerkin schemes in time. Projected auxiliary variables for Hamiltonian derivatives are necessary for exact energy conservation. We provide an iterative solver approach based on monolithic patch smoothers, which allows us to efficiently converge a Newton method sufficiently that energy errors due to the solver are very small. We extend this construction to the energy conserving Stochastic Forcing by Lie Transport formulation. Then we demonstrate the convergence, conservation and robustness in numerical tests.

offered.title: ADER-ZIST - a mixed explicit ADER-DG and zonally implicit space-time DG approach for Cartesian cut cell meshes
offered.abstract: We present high order accurate mixed explicit-implicit discontinuous Galerkin (DG) schemes for the solution of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws on Cartesian cut cell meshes. Such meshes may contain arbitrarily small cut cells, which leads to the well-known small cell problem: the CFL condition of explicit schemes would severely restrict the admissible time step. To overcome this difficulty, we use high order explicit fully-discrete one-step ADER-DG schemes only on Cartesian cells away from the embedded boundaries. The zone close to the embedded boundary, which consists of cut cells and their direct face neighbors, is discretized with an implicit space-time DG scheme that is coupled to the explicit scheme directly via the numerical flux. The resulting scheme, called ADER-ZIST (ADER-DG with Zonally Implicit Space-Time DG), is conservative by construction, and its time step is determined only by the size of the Cartesian background cells. Curved embedded boundaries are represented by high order isoparametric sub-triangles inside the cut cells, and the nonlinear system of the implicit cells is solved via an inexact matrix-free Newton-Krylov method. For problems with shock waves, we add an artificial viscosity term whose strength is controlled by an oscillation-eliminating smoothness sensor. ADER-ZIST is assessed on a comprehensive set of test problems for the compressible Euler equations, ranging from smooth flows around straight and curved embedded boundaries to acoustic scattering and shock-dominated flows. The scheme essentially reaches its nominal order of accuracy N+1 for smooth solutions and for polynomial degrees up to N=5, on meshes with minimal volume fractions of the small cut cells down to the order of 10^-7.

offered.title: Targeted Entropy-Stable Nonlinear Artificial Dissipation for High-Order Spectral-Element Summation-By-Parts Discretizations
offered.abstract: Artificial dissipation improves the robustness of high-order methods for under-resolved flows, but can compromise accuracy and suppress physically relevant structures if its strength and spatial distribution are not appropriately controlled. We present a sensor-activated nonlinear artificial-dissipation framework, inspired by the residual correction method, for continuous and discontinuous summation-by-parts discretizations. In contrast to many existing spectral-element dissipation operators that either reduce the formal order of accuracy or target only the highest polynomial modes, the proposed framework permits design- and higher-order dissipation with explicit control over its magnitude, spatial distribution, activation, and convergence rate under mesh refinement. This modular construction also recovers several existing methods through appropriate choices of its components. The dissipation preserves discrete conservation and semidiscrete entropy stability whenever the base method satisfies these properties. It is dimensionally consistent, element local, and discretization agnostic, as the added term is constructed independently of the base spatial residual. For smooth solutions under suitable mesh assumptions, we establish parameter choices that retain the formal accuracy of the base discretization. Numerical experiments with summation-by-parts discretizations of the Burgers and Euler equations demonstrate substantially improved robustness for under-resolved flows and flows with shock waves while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth solutions, using the same parameter choices across several test problems. Overall, these results show that targeted dissipation can improve the robustness of high-order methods without excessive damping of resolved flow structures.

offered.title: Preconditioning proximal Galerkin: mesh and degree robust solvers for variational inequalities
offered.abstract: The proximal Galerkin algorithm is a structure-preserving solver for variational inequalities that results in discretization-independent nonlinear iteration counts. However, in large three-dimensional simulations, the arising Newton saddle point systems cannot be feasibly solved by direct methods. To leverage an iterative linear solver, we propose a robust and scalable block preconditioner. Instead of using the usual dual Schur complement that acts on the latent variable, we design a preconditioner for the primal Schur complement. This leads to a block preconditioner that requires two approximate inverses of the latent block and only one of the primal Schur complement. The latent block represents an algebraic equation which, after a small perturbation, can be cheaply inverted. We then introduce two choices of approximations for the primal Schur complement: a PDE-operator-based and an algebraic approach. Either approximation can be efficiently inverted by geometric multigrid. We investigate the effectiveness of these strategies when proximal Galerkin is applied to obstacle, Signorini, and strain-constrained elasticity problems and also compare with a monolithic multigrid approach. Choices of standard relaxation methods, in the block preconditioner route, lead to robust iteration counts with respect to the mesh size and discretization degree. Moreover, in the context of the Signorini, specialized relaxation and prolongation also result in effective solvers for nearly-incompressible elastic materials. The linear solves are parameter-robust in 2D, with only mild growth in 3D. This allows for the solution of a three-dimensional contact problem, with a Poisson's ratio of 0.499, discretized with over ten million degrees of freedom.

offered.title: Fully discrete multi-entropy-stable compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
offered.abstract: We develop fully discrete multi-entropy-stable high-order compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin (cRKDG) methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. Our main result is a weak cell entropy inequality for multi-dimensional systems after one full high-order Runge--Kutta (RK) time step. The proof exploits the cell-local intermediate stages of cRKDG: their perturbations are controlled by the initial in-cell variation. The analysis does not require a strong stability preserving decomposition or stagewise entropy correction. For a sufficiently dissipative Lax--Friedrichs flux and explicit RK methods with nonnegative output weights, the inequality holds under a suitable time-step restriction for strongly convex entropy pairs. For a prescribed, uniformly conditioned family of such entropies, common dissipation and time-step conditions ensure weak cell entropy stability for all entropy pairs. A single cell-average-preserving scaling at the end of each step then enforces all corresponding strong cell entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also prove a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem: under the stated assumptions, any strongly convergent sequence of numerical solutions converges to a weak solution satisfying all prescribed entropy inequalities. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate high-order accuracy, the benefit of multiple entropy constraints for nonconvex scalar problems, and robust performance on shock problems.

overviews.overview: This period splits between conservative discretizations for transport-type PDEs and methods that adapt to singular structure or optimization hardness. On the PDE side, a mixed explicit/implicit ADER-DG scheme for Cartesian cut-cell meshes removes the small-cell CFL bottleneck by treating the boundary layer of cut cells with implicit space-time DG while keeping the rest explicit, with conservation built in and artificial viscosity added only near shocks [2610.13245]. A companion line of work pushes finite-volume methods as a local-balance framework on arbitrary meshes [2610.19748]. For fractional terminal problems, a nonstandard Jacobi pseudospectral basis is tailored to weak endpoint singularities, with existence, uniqueness, and convergence proved without mesh grading [2610.20829]. In a different direction, ReLU matrix decomposition is shown NP-hard even for binary matrices and rank one, and the Frobenius formulation can be ill-posed [2610.22255].

picks.hook: A fractional pseudospectral construction built around endpoint-weighted Jacobi bases, with convergence theory that explicitly matches terminal singularities instead of smoothing them away.
The first complexity and well-posedness results for ReLU matrix decomposition, including NP-hardness at rank one and a geometric view of exact decompositions.

offered.title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
offered.abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

offered.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
offered.abstract: We consider the problem of model order reduction (MOR) in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). We prove generalizations of well-known necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models, originally stated for rational functions in $H_2$ Hardy-Hilbert spaces. We construct an alternative to the iterative rational Krylov (IRKA) algorithm for RKHSs with differentiable kernels to obtain norm-optimal reduced-order models. Then, we introduce generalized Malmquist-Takenaka (GMT) functions that can be used to define orthonormal bases in an arbitrary RKHS. Using GMT functions, we propose unitary transformations between separable RKHSs. This allows us to extend our optimality conditions and subsequent algorithms to MOR problems posed in RKHSs with non-differentiable kernels. The potential and versatility of the proposed MOR framework is demonstrated in several numerical experiments. We perform norm-optimal MOR on various machine learning models such as support vector machines and deep ReLU networks. In addition, we show how the proposed MOR framework can be used to solve seemingly unrelated problems. In particular, we provide an example for fitting high degree polynomials to data and also obtain a FEM-like method for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with an optimal kernel basis.

offered.title: KernelPack-JAX: a meshless differentiable GPU framework for node generation and forward and inverse PDE problems
offered.abstract: We present KernelPack-JAX, a meshless, differentiable, GPU framework in JAX for solving forward and inverse PDE problems in domains whose boundaries, including internal obstacles, are given only by samples of their smooth pieces. Our node generator is based on a new stacked representation of piecewise-smooth boundaries, in which a parametric partition of unity of each smooth piece induces the supports of a curl-free implicit partition of unity of the whole boundary. This representation keeps the edges and corners of the boundary and classifies every point of space without a global fit. Boundary and interior nodes are then selected by a parallel greedy independent-set algorithm that reproduces sequential Poisson-disk sampling exactly. We discretize elliptic and parabolic problems with radial basis function-generated finite differences (RBF-FD) on stencils selected by a new visibility heuristic to avoid crossing the boundary, with ghost nodes for the boundary conditions. In addition, our framework exposes a GPU sparse direct solver to JAX as a differentiable linear solve, so that Jacobians of time-dependent problems cost a small multiple of a forward solve. We derive error estimates that separate consistency from stability and bound the parameter error by the forward error. We demonstrate high-order convergence for Darcy flow, reaction-diffusion, and advection-diffusion in 2D and 3D domains, including one with an internal obstacle, and show that the recovered parameters largely follow the forward errors. We also present timings for every stage.

offered.title: Generalized MLS and LS-SVR for Allen-Cahn Equations on Spheres
offered.abstract: This work extends least-squares support vector regression (LS-SVR) based on the generalized moving least squares (GMLS) approximation to the numerical solution of partial differential equations on spheres. We show that the proposed approach constructs a kernel-based approximant in its dual form and establishes its connection with the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Furthermore, solving the PDE through the proposed LS-SVR framework is shown to be equivalent to solving a smoothing problem or a kernel ridge regression problem in the corresponding RKHS. As applications, the method is employed to solve the Allen-Cahn equation and its conservative counterpart on spheres. An implicit first-order operator-splitting scheme is used to separate each model into linear and nonlinear subproblems. The linear subproblem is discretized by the backward differentiation formula and approximated at each time step using LS-SVR derived from a GMLS-based collocation formulation, while the nonlinear part is treated analytically. The resulting scheme is shown to admit a unique numerical solution at every time step. For the conservative Allen-Cahn model, a correction procedure is incorporated to preserve mass. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed framework.

offered.title: Data-dependent Compact Multinode Shepard Method
offered.abstract: We introduce a data-dependent compact multinode Shepard method for the approximation of scattered multivariate data. The proposed approach extends the compact multinode Shepard operator by incorporating nonlinear, data-dependent weights inspired by the weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) methodology while preserving the partition of unity structure and the locality of the approximation. The construction is based on compactly supported multinode weight functions associated with local polynomial interpolants defined on unisolvent stencils. A smoothness indicator is employed to adapt the contribution of each stencil according to the local regularity of the underlying function, thereby reducing spurious oscillations near discontinuities while retaining the optimal approximation order in smooth regions. We establish the theoretical approximation properties of the proposed operator: it achieves the order of accuracy of its linear counterpart for sufficiently smooth functions and, under an explicit indicator-separation hypothesis, the same order is retained at every covered evaluation point near a jump discontinuity. Numerical experiments for local degrees up to four illustrate the performance of the method on both smooth and non-smooth data, on scattered as well as on gridded nodes.

offered.title: Simultaneous Matrix Multiplication by Tensor Contraction Aggregation
offered.abstract: We present an interpretation of the fast matrix multiplication algorithms of Coppersmith and Winograd as aggregations of tensor contractions. This point of view provides a direct connection to older constructions by Pan and to more recent work on bilinear algorithms for symmetric tensor contraction. Further, we provide a new simple approach for exact aggregation of tensor contractions, each one yielding an independent matrix-matrix product. These constructions and border rank adaptations thereof do not come close to improving the best known bounds on $ω$ (the matrix multiplication exponent), but provide explicit moderate-size fast matrix multiplication algorithms that achieve a better exponent than Strassen's algorithm and have potential practical value. These results imply improvements to the best known bounds on the rank and border rank of a fixed number of independent square matrix products. In particular, using $\langle m,m,m\rangle$ to denote the matrix multiplication tensor for matrices of dimension $m$, we obtain constructions that give bounds such as the border rank bound \[ \underline R\!\left(\langle n^2,n^2,n^2\rangle^{\oplus9}\right) \le (n+1)^6+6(n+1)^5, \] and the exact rank bound \[ R\!\left(\langle n^3,n^3,n^3\rangle^{\oplus14}\right)\le (n+1)^9. \] We quantify the accuracy of such constructions in finite precision, and provide border-rank constructions that reduce cost with limiting retained fractions of accuracy at least $1/2$, $1/3$, or $1/4$ relative to the classical matrix-multiplication approach under the stated error model.

offered.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions
offered.abstract: Solutions of second-order elliptic PDE problems on nonconvex or cracked domains with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions typically lie outside $H^2(Ω)$. Near re-entrant corners, crack tips and points where the boundary condition changes type, the gradient grows like $r^{λ-1}$ with $λ<1$. We study residual-based adaptive refinement in hybrid variational-collocation PINNs. A multiscale Fourier-feature network is trained on a composite loss. The loss combines a variational residual tested against Legendre bubble functions, a strong-form collocation term and penalties for the Dirichlet and Neumann data. The variational term needs only first derivatives of the network, whereas the collocation term requires second derivatives and provides a residual that can be evaluated at any point. After each training stage, candidate points selected by this residual are added to the collocation set. The method is tested on five two dimensional benchmarks, namely a Mode~III crack, a cross-shaped domain with four re-entrant corners with unequal amplitude, a reaction-diffusion problem with four localized peaks, a monotone semilinear problem with a boundary layer and the Motz problem. Compared with uniform point insertion under the same collocation and iteration budget, residual-based refinement reduced the relative $L^2$ error by up to a factor of $32$, the relative $L^\infty$ error by up to a factor of $38$ and the relative $H^1$ semi-norm error by up to a factor of $15$.

offered.title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster
offered.abstract: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration. For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.

offered.title: Study of the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method -- The Laplacian data assimilation case
offered.abstract: We investigate the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method, in the context of the data assimilation problem for the Laplacian. We provide error estimates explicit in all the parameters appearing in the model and the method (i.e. the amplitude of noise, the size mesh, the regularization parameter and the number of iterations of the method). This allows to devise strategies to choose the aforementioned parameters, for example to guarantee convergence of the method when the level of noise goes to zero. Numerical experiments on a two-dimensional problem are provided, illustrating the relevance of the obtained estimates.

offered.title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: FFT-Based Fast Algorithms and Joint Rotation--Translation Pose Denoising
offered.abstract: Rigid-body pose signals couple rotation and translation, yet most existing denoising pipelines treat them separately and analyse them only in the Fourier domain. We show that this separation is unnecessary and often suboptimal. We fuse dual quaternions, which encode rotation and translation in a single singularity-free algebra, with linear canonical transforms, which supply flexible quadratic-phase analysis, to develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) with an explicit kernel ordering. We establish inverse and energy-preservation properties, structured spatial and frequency convolution relations, and, crucially, fast algorithms built on complex FFTs. These algorithms make the DQ-DLCT practical: a two-stage chirp-adaptive scheme then performs joint rotation--translation denoising in a single transform domain. Numerical experiments confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the fast transform and demonstrate strong denoising performance on measured pose sequences and constructed two-dimensional pose fields. The DQ-DLCT thus turns a heavy algebraic construction into a deployable tool for pose signal processing.

offered.title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows
offered.abstract: Low-NFE generative ODE sampling is constrained not only by solver order, but also by how a fixed budget of network evaluations is distributed along the flow. We develop a density-level backward-error framework that identifies the component of a solver's modified-equation defect that changes the evolving marginal, while excluding solenoidal trajectory distortion that is invisible in Wasserstein tangent geometry. The resulting residual induces a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and, through gauge freedom, an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity representatives of the same density path. This separates our approach from schedule search driven by trajectory or endpoint surrogates and from higher-order solver design. Exact Gaussian and mixture models establish the mechanism, including cases where curvature-based allocation fails and continuum-optimal transport is not discretization-optimal. On a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM probability-flow ODE, density-aware allocation consistently improves fixed-update Euler sampling in the low-NFE regime. Matched-seed convergence to a dense Euler reference confirms that the method accelerates approximation of the same high-NFE flow rather than changing the asymptotic sampler.

offered.title: Beyond exponential tilting: sharp asymptotics and improved importance sampling for rare events
offered.abstract: A classical approach for importance sampling (IS) of a rare event is to tilt the measure using its large deviation minimizer, thereby shifting the proposal mean towards the event set. While this tilt is log-efficient, we show that the coefficient of variation of the resulting estimator still grows like $\varepsilon^{-1/4}$ in the small-noise limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Motivated by sharp large deviation asymptotics and the local geometry of the event set at the minimizer, we propose improvements using a control variate or an anisotropic, non-Gaussian proposal. We prove, up to truncations that hold with high probability, and confirm empirically in high-dimensional examples, that the former bounds the coefficient of variation and the latter makes it vanish, so that a bounded number of samples suffices. Our analysis addresses both the coefficient of variation of the different proposals and their necessary and sufficient sample size based on the Kullback--Leibler divergence of the IS target from the proposal; both yield the same rates in $\varepsilon$. We demonstrate the resulting samplers, including a variant that blends the classical and the new proposal across noise levels, for a stochastic Korteweg--de Vries equation with thousands of random inputs.

offered.title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
offered.abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

offered.title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
offered.abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs. The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.

offered.title: Sequential Monte Carlo Sampling of Feasible Regions Represented by R-Functions
offered.abstract: Feasible-region sampling and volume estimation become increasingly inefficient when constraints define only a small fraction of a convenient bounding domain. We combine R-functions, which encode compound feasibility as a continuous signed field, with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) samplers. The proposed construction exploits not only the sign of the R-function, which determines exact feasibility, but also its continuous negative values outside the feasible set, which provide graded information on constraint violation. Logistic intermediate distributions use this information to guide particles progressively towards feasibility, while the final target distribution remains uniform on the feasible region. Experiments on intersections and unions, including disconnected cases of hyperballs, show substantial variance reductions relative to direct rejection sampling, with the statistical advantage generally increasing as the feasible fraction decreases. For sufficiently small feasible regions, these advantages persist even after accounting for computational cost. To isolate the benefit of continuous R-function information, we also compare the proposed method with an SMC sampler with a region-only (RO) construction that uses the same sequential particle machinery but retains only binary feasible/infeasible information. We demonstrate that the R-function-informed SMC method concentrates particles in the feasible region earlier and produces lower-variance volume estimates than RO.

offered.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo based meshfree methods for parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds
offered.abstract: We develop and analyze a randomized path sampling framework for the pointwise approximation of linear parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds, treating both closed manifolds and manifolds with Dirichlet boundary. Based on the Feynman-Kac representation, we construct a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization, referred to as the p-Ret scheme, for the manifold diffusion generated by the uniformly elliptic operator, and use it to formulate the Monte Carlo (MC) and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) methods. We derive the local weak consistency of the p-Ret transition and first-order weak convergence of the temporal discretization on closed manifolds. For fixed $h$, we show that RQMC sampling yields asymptotically faster variance decay than standard MC. On closed manifolds, the variance is $o(n^{-1})$ and, under additional regularity, satisfies the sharper bound $O(n^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. For Dirichlet problems, despite the discontinuities induced by numerical first exit, nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling attains $O(n^{-1-1/s+\varepsilon})$ variance for any $\varepsilon>0$ under suitable regularity assumptions, where $s$ denotes the nominal path-space dimension. More notably, we further develop an Array-RQMC strategy based on stepwise low-dimensional randomized point sets and a Hilbert space-filling curve that maps high-dimensional particle states to a one-dimensional ordering, and establish a variance rate of $o(n^{-1})$ under suitable assumptions. Numerical results demonstrate that both RQMC methods reduce variance and root mean square error (RMSE) relative to standard MC and remain effective for manifolds with intrinsic dimension up to $50$.

offered.title: Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
offered.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.

offered.title: Stability and Error Estimates for Convolution Quadrature under Radial Symbol Bounds
offered.abstract: We develop stability and error estimates for multistep convolution quadrature (CQ) under general radial bounds on the Laplace symbol. Instead of the classical single-power condition $|F(z)|\leq M|z|^{-μ}$, we assume $|F(z)|\leq CΦ(|z|)$ and consider two classes of radial functions: monotone bounds satisfying a scaling condition and regularly varying bounds with locally bounded above and away from zero. For strongly $A(α)$-stable multistep methods, we derive approximation and stability estimates for the CQ weights, as well as error bounds for power-type inputs $g_β(t)=t^{β-1}/Γ(β)$ with $β>0$. These estimates explicitly retain the dependence on the memory law through the factor $Φ(t_n^{-1})$. The framework accommodates symbols whose behavior cannot be described by a global single-power. It also preserves slowly varying and multiscale factors that would be lost under a coarser power majorant. The theory is applied to fractional viscoelastic models, distributed-order operators, and logarithmic-power memory operators. Numerical experiments with backward Euler and second-order backward differentiation CQ confirm the expected temporal convergence orders for direct responses. Complementary evolution examples demonstrate the corresponding temporal behavior for smooth and nonsmooth initial data.

offered.title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
offered.abstract: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $Φ_t=F_θ^{-1}\circΨ_t\circ F_θ$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $Ψ_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_θ$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $Ψ$. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving $F_θ$ cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to $|f|$ and sampled log-uniformly in $|x|$ around an equilibrium, with the anchors $F_θ(0)=0$, $DF_θ(0)=I$; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation $8.3\times10^{-3}$ and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of $F_θ$.

offered.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
offered.abstract: We develop the first tensor-product sparse-grid finite element discretizations of Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. We construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to full grids.

offered.title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
offered.abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

offered.title: DSINC beyond Heston: the 3/2 and other non-affine stochastic-volatility models
offered.abstract: This paper extends the damped-sinc (DSINC) method for American options beyond the affine Heston class to general one-factor stochastic-volatility models. We show that the collapse identity, which reduces the early-exercise integral to a single spectral integral, remains valid for these models. Damping between zero and one is admissible whenever the discounted spot is a nonnegative local martingale. An Itô transformation of the volatility factorizes the conditional characteristic function and identifies a natural coordinate for approximating the exercise boundary. The 3/2 model admits closed-form joint transforms in terms of Kummer functions, while uncorrelated SABR admits a Bessel representation. When a practical closed-form transform is unavailable, the required volatility integral is computed directly by solving one backward equation per frequency, without a grid in the log-price. Through a known change of volatility coordinate, this approach also accommodates correlated SABR. Tests on the 3/2, SABR, GARCH and lognormal-volatility models show agreement with fine finite-difference benchmarks to within one basis point of the strike. Computational cost is comparable to or lower than that of our finite-difference implementation, except for the slower Hankel implementation of uncorrelated SABR.

offered.title: Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure
offered.abstract: In this work, we study numerical approximations of the equation \begin{equation} \partial_t^αu-\nabla\cdot\left(u^{m-1}\nabla(-Δ)^{-σ}u\right)=0, \end{equation} where $0<α<1$, $0<σ<1$ and $m>1$. The Caputo derivative is discretized by the L1 formula, while the nonlinear nonlocal flux is approximated by a conservative upwind finite-difference scheme. We establish several structural properties of the implicit scheme in arbitrary space dimension, including a discrete maximum principle, non-negativity, mass conservation, $\ell^\infty$ and $\ell^2$ stability, existence of non-negative discrete solutions, and a discrete energy-dissipation estimate. Our assumptions include natural symmetry, a sign condition on the sum of the directional coefficients, and decay on the discrete weights. We also derive a consistency estimate for the complete nonlinear spatial operator. For rigorous convergence analysis, we restrict ourselves to one space dimension and introduce the cumulative variable associated with the density. This transforms the discrete problem into a monotone approximation of an equation involving the fractional Laplacian. Interestingly, for semigroup-based pressure-gradient weights, the resulting discrete operator is identified with the fractional discrete Laplacian. Next, using comparison and contraction properties of the integrated scheme, for $m\geq2$ and under the stated spatial regularity and weighted temporal consistency assumptions, we prove uniform convergence of the cumulative numerical solution and convergence of the corresponding density against compactly supported smooth test functions. The temporal estimates allow a weak singularity at the initial time. We also analyze an explicit variant of the scheme and derive a sufficient CFL condition covering the full range $0<σ<1$.

offered.title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
offered.abstract: We propose two families of multigrid preconditioners for unfitted finite element discretisations of the Riesz maps of the de Rham complex, in H(grad), H(curl) and H(div), stabilised by cell aggregation. The first is a geometric multigrid method applied directly to the unfitted operators, on a hierarchy of background meshes that share the same boundary representation. Its smoothers are star patches built on the aggregated mesh, so that each patch captures the kernel of the stabilisation. The second is a multilevel auxiliary-space preconditioner that combines a patch smoother localised around the cut cells with the body-fitted problem on the active mesh, which is in turn solved by a non-nested geometric multigrid method. Both are used as building blocks of block-diagonal preconditioners for the mixed Hodge Laplacians. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on geometries with a controlled cut fraction and on general geometries, show iteration counts that are robust with respect to the cut configuration, the mesh size and the number of levels. We also report results for higher-order discretisations, weakly imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions and a face-based stabilisation.

offered.title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
offered.abstract: We construct and analyse a fully discrete scheme for a Kirchhoff-type nonlinear integro-differential equation in two spatial dimensions with time-dependent coefficients. The scheme combines a symmetric three-layer time discretization of Crank--Nicolson type with a conforming finite element method of arbitrary polynomial degree $p$ and a Picard iteration for the nonlinearity. We prove that the Picard iteration is well defined and, that the iterates converge to the Ritz projection of the exact solution measured in fractional-power norms of the discrete Laplacian. Running the same energy argument in the unshifted norms, and under the same hypotheses, we then obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p+1} + τ^2 )$ in $L^2$ and $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p} + τ^2 )$ in $H^1$ for the full error. For the homogeneous problem with constant coefficients, the exact solution of the scheme moreover preserves a discrete energy identically. Numerical experiments with manufactured solutions reproduce the predicted second order in time and the full spatial order $h^{p+1}$ in the $L^2$-norm.

overviews.overview: This period’s numerical analysis papers lean toward adaptive, kernel-based, and structure-aware discretizations. One line uses optimization-driven adaptive Chebyshev patches to recover self-similar singularity profiles, eliminating far-field truncation and reaching O(10^-14) accuracy for Burgers profiles, with residuals as low as O(10^-14) to O(10^-10) on the generalized De Gregorio family and O(10^-8) locally for 2D Boussinesq [2610.30492]. Another develops meshless GPU PDE solvers with differentiable node generation and RBF-FD stencils, reporting high-order convergence for Darcy, reaction-diffusion, and advection-diffusion in 2D and 3D [2610.25484]. Kernel and RKHS ideas also reappear in norm-optimal model reduction, while WENO-like data-dependent weights extend compact Shepard approximation to jumps without losing smooth-region order [2610.31026].

picks.hook: Best entry point if you care about singular PDE structure: it combines adaptive Chebyshev patches, asymptotic patches, and Gauss-Newton/LM optimization to recover profiles with near machine precision.
Worth reading for a practical meshless pipeline: it couples boundary-aware node generation, RBF-FD discretization, and differentiable sparse direct solves on GPU for forward and inverse PDEs.

offered.title: A Local Stabilized Isogeometric Formulation with Discontinuous Pressure for Mesh-Conforming and Immersed Analysis of Nearly Incompressible Elasticity
offered.abstract: Nearly incompressible materials arise in soft tissues, elastomers, gels, and other soft solids. Yet, numerical modeling remains challenging because displacement-based formulations can exhibit volumetric locking near incompressibility. Mixed displacement-pressure formulations address this difficulty but require compatible approximation spaces satisfying the inf-sup condition. In mixed formulations, discontinuous pressure spaces are attractive since pressure degrees of freedom can be condensed locally. In high-order isogeometric analysis, however, their Galerkin stability requires pressure-grid coarsening that increases with polynomial degree. Here, we develop a variational multiscale (VMS) stabilized mixed isogeometric formulation that retains this locality while substantially relaxing the restriction. The key observation is that VMS stabilization controls nonconstant elementwise pressure modes and is unconditionally stable with respect to its parameter, provided the elementwise constant pressure component satisfies the inf-sup condition. Consequently, for maximally continuous displacement splines, a pressure grid coarsened by a factor of two satisfies the constant-mode inf-sup criterion independently of polynomial degree. Local condensation then yields a displacement-only system, facilitating use in existing displacement solvers. The formulation is further extended to immersed isogeometric analysis with extended B-splines, pressure-cell aggregation, subdivision-based cut-cell quadrature, and weak enforcement of essential boundary conditions. Discrete inf-sup studies and convergence analyses in the Kirsch and Cook's membrane benchmarks demonstrate stability and show that the immersed treatment preserves mixed stability properties. The proposed framework therefore provides a local, high-order, and robust approach for nearly incompressible problems in mesh-conforming and immersed settings.

offered.title: Higher-Order QMC $hp$-FEM UQ for Singular Perturbation: Reaction-Diffusion with Gevrey-Parametric Reaction Coefficient
offered.abstract: We analyze the combined discretization of singularly perturbed reaction-diffusion problems with perturbation parameter $\varepsilon\in (0,1]$ and with parametric, Gevrey-regular reaction term, by $hp$-Galerkin FE methods and by higher-order polynomial lattice rules. We establish $\varepsilon$-robust algebraic convergence rates for the combined QMC $hp$-FEM approximation that are not subject to the curse of dimensionality (CoD) in the parametric reaction coefficient, and only limited by the sparsity and the $\mathfrak{s}_{y}$-Gevrey regularity of the reaction coefficient expansion. On the interval $(-1,1)$, we establish an $\varepsilon$-robust, root-exponential convergence rate $\exp(-σ\, p_{\mathrm{FE}}^{1/\mathfrak{s}_{x}})$ for $hp$-Galerkin FEM for reaction-diffusion problems under $\mathfrak{s}_{x}$-Gevrey regularity assumptions on the reaction coefficient and the source term, a result that can be of independent interest. Numerical experiments are consistent with the theoretical bounds.

offered.title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
offered.abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.

offered.title: Model reduction in time: Learning flow maps for reducing stochastic dynamical systems in time
offered.abstract: Predictions with dynamical systems can be computationally expensive---even with reduced models---because reaching future prediction times can require many sequential time integration steps. We propose Flow-Map First-Order Trajectory Matching (FM-FTM), a nonintrusive model reduction approach that accelerates ensemble predictions of stochastic dynamical systems by learning flow maps that replace multiple time-integration steps. Our method uses first-order trajectory matching (FTM) to learn a deterministic representation of the stochastic probability-current dynamics and then reduces its evolution over time into a flow map whose evaluation directly yields predictions over long time horizons. Numerical experiments on evolution problems with stochastic forcing demonstrate that FM-FTM accelerates ensemble predictions by up to two orders of magnitude while accurately predicting time marginals and ensemble statistics.

offered.title: Randomized Symplectic Model Reduction: One-Pass Basis Construction and Sketched Hamiltonian Assembly
offered.abstract: Symplectic model order reduction of Hamiltonian systems yields reduced dynamics that conserve the reduced Hamiltonian along exact trajectories, avoiding the artificial energy drift that can arise from conventional projection methods. For large-scale spatial discretizations, however, basis construction and reduced-operator assembly can involve substantial offline costs. Randomized numerical linear algebra can reduce these costs through low-dimensional sketches while supporting streaming and parallel implementations. We develop randomized techniques for two parts of the offline stage while preserving the Hamiltonian structure of the reduced dynamics. First, we introduce the one-pass sketched randomized cSVD (Ops-rcSVD), a one-pass randomized variant of the complex-SVD algorithm. Combining randomized range finding with an independent left sketch, Ops-rcSVD constructs an ortho-symplectic reduced basis from a single pass over the snapshot ensemble. Second, for quadratic Hamiltonian systems, we introduce a randomized reduced-Hamiltonian assembly based on sketching the reduced basis and operator actions, yielding a reduced Hamiltonian system by construction. We derive bounds for the snapshot projection error, uniform-in-parameter perturbation bounds for the sketched reduced Hamiltonian, and an energy-norm estimate for the difference between reduced and sketched reduced trajectories. Experiments on large-scale systems show that Ops-rcSVD attains projection accuracy comparable to deterministic and two-pass randomized constructions while reducing basis-construction time. They further demonstrate accurate sketched reduced-Hamiltonian assembly when storing the complete snapshot ensemble is no longer feasible.

offered.title: Matrix Nearness Problems Revisited
offered.abstract: Given a nonempty set of matrices $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$ and a matrix $A \not\in\mathcal{E}$, a matrix nearness problem (or matrix distance problem) consists in finding a matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ that is closest to $A$, in some norm, as well as the corresponding distance. This article is a survey of matrix nearness problems and of numerical algorithms for their solution. We pay special attention to modern related topics, such as Riemannian optimization and pseudospectra, that were not discussed in depth in previous reviews about this topic. Besides collecting known facts, we also prove some foundational results that, at least in the present form, we could not locate in the literature.

offered.title: Integer-Quantized Hierarchical Matrices with Adaptive Bit Allocation
offered.abstract: We present an adaptive bitwidth allocation method for quantizing low-rank factors in hierarchical matrices in order to decrease storage while meeting a given constraint on their reconstruction error. For the bitwidth allocation we formulate a discrete storage minimization problem and show that an optimal assignment can give larger singular values at least as many bits as smaller ones. We further develop a greedy algorithm that meets the specified max-norm quantization error budget. We investigate a hierarchical block partition in which all of the non-diagonal blocks are represented by quantized low-rank factors and only dense blocks remain dense; in this way a global reconstruction bound related to $η_k$ and $R_k$ is obtained, with the former and latter being bounds on the truncation and reconstruction arithmetic errors, respectively. Extensive simulations, carried out with kernel and BEM matrices under block-relative budgets, indicate that the proposed method achieves a reduction in storage of up to $44.3\times$ when compared to storing the complete matrix densely in FP64, and a reduction of up to $5.70\times$ when compared to the FP64 low-rank factors within the same partition, together with measured reconstruction errors that remained below the maximum norm bounds in all the hierarchical tests.

offered.title: A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
offered.abstract: This paper develops reliable a posteriori error estimates for finite element approximation of an evolution equation with a positive-type memory kernels on bounded convex polygonal or polyhedral domains, including both smooth and weakly singular kernels. For the weakly singular kernel $t^{α-1}/Γ(α),\; 0<α<1,$ the model captures the transition from parabolic diffusion to wave propagation, recovering the corresponding limiting equations as $α\to0^+$ and $α\to1^-$, respectively, with the memory term governing the intermediate dynamics. The spatial discretization employs time-dependent finite element spaces, while the backward Euler method combined with numerical quadrature is used for time integration. A unified \emph{a posteriori} analysis is established for both semidiscrete and fully discrete approximations. Elliptic reconstruction yields optimal spatial error estimates, while a memory-lag estimate preserves the essential cancellation in the convolution term, yielding a first-order temporal estimator whose kernel dependence is characterized by its integral. The resulting estimators are robust, with constants independent of the final time, spatial mesh size, and time step. Their kernel dependence involves only computable quantities, avoiding exponential growth in time. Moreover, for the weakly singular kernel, the $α$-dependent factors remain uniformly bounded for $α\in(0,1).$ Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the theoretical results, and a space-time adaptive algorithm is also demonstrated on an L-shaped domain featuring a corner singularity and two temporal layers.

offered.title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
offered.abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive low-resolution particles (reduced-order surrogates constructed via intrusive Galerkin projection). These surrogates act as control variates to enhance the statistical estimate of the full-order posterior, yielding enhanced analysis accuracy at comparable computational cost. The work focuses on two particle flows based on log homotopy, the stochastic Gromov flow and deterministic Exact flow. Numerical experiments with the Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) and Quasi-Geostrophic (QG) test problems demonstrate that the proposed MFPFF achieves accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations while significantly reducing computational expense.

offered.title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
offered.abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

offered.title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
offered.abstract: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|ξ|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.

offered.title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
offered.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme to approximate solutions to the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (iLLG) equation, a state-of-the-art model to describe the dynamics of the magnetization at subpicosecond time scales. The method employs first-order finite elements for the spatial discretization and the two-step backward differentiation formula (BDF2) for the time discretization, where the inertial term is treated by a convex combination of BDF2 and the backward Euler method. We prove well-posedness and unconditional stability of the scheme, and obtain explicit bounds for the error in the realization of the iLLG-inherent unit length constraint satisfied by the magnetization. Moreover, we derive the discrete energy law satisfied by the approximations, which resembles the inherent dissipative energy law of the model. Finally, with a constructive approach, we prove unconditional convergence of the approximations toward a weak solution of the problem. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the scheme and validate the theoretical findings.

offered.title: Weak adversarial tensor neural network for high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equations
offered.abstract: Solving high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck (SFP) equations remains challenging. Recently, deep learning methods have shown great potential for solving high-dimensional SFP equations due to their universal approximation and mesh-free training. However, the high-dimensional integrals involved in loss computation and normalization can be expensive to approximate accurately using Monte Carlo integration. To address this issue, we propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method for solving high-dimensional SFP equations, which combines a weak adversarial (WA) formulation with the tensor neural network (TNN). The WA formulation avoids the cross terms introduced by squaring the strong residual, reducing the number of integrals to be computed. When both the primal network and the adversarial test network are set as TNNs, the TNN quadrature scheme provides accurate and efficient normalization and loss computation with relatively few fixed quadrature points, avoiding the statistical sampling error that arises when using Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the effectiveness numerically on four high-dimensional SFP equations. For the 6D unimodal, 6D multi-modal, 10D multi-modal and 20D multi-modal problems, WATNN achieves the mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% respectively, in only a few minutes.

offered.title: A framework for trackable and modular rounding error analysis
offered.abstract: Robust and meaningful rounding error analysis is becoming increasingly challenging as modern numerical computations involve a rapidly evolving variety of arithmetic formats, precisions, and computational kernels. We propose a trackable and modular framework for rounding error analysis, together with a new notation for bounding accumulated rounding errors. The analysis is trackable in the sense that the origin and propagation of individual error terms remain explicit in the final result, and modular in the sense that local error bounds can be replaced according to the arithmetic, precision, or computational kernel without repeating the structural analysis. We also introduce the notation $γ_n=(1-{\bm u})^{-n}-1$, which provides an alternative to the classical $γ_n^{\mathrm h}=n{\bm u}/(1-n{\bm u})$ notation. A key feature is that our notation does not require the restriction $n{\bm u}<1$ and conveniently handles errors arising from division. Using block LU factorization as a representative example, we show that the framework distinguishes the error sources of different algorithmic variants and permits improved kernels, such as compensated summation and accurate matrix multiplication, to be incorporated directly into the resulting error bounds.

offered.title: Characterization of the Tau Spectrum for Eigenvalue Problems
offered.abstract: We consider tau approximations of a general eigenvalue problem for a $K$-th-order linear differential operator in one dimension, and we show that the approximate spectrum satisfies a resolvent-based spectral determinant property, which we use to investigate it. More specifically, we analyze the spectral determinant property for a second-order Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue problem approximated using Gegenbauer tau methods. Notably, a quantitative error analysis identifies two values of the Gegenbauer parameter $γ$ leading to better approximation properties. These values correspond to Legendre polynomials and their derivatives. Moreover, we discuss the behavior of the largest eigenvalue of the tau approximation. The results are validated with a numerical implementation.

offered.title: Multifidelity variational inference for derivative-free PDE-constrained inverse problems
offered.abstract: We develop a multifidelity black-box variational inference (MF-BBVI) approach for PDE-constrained Bayesian inverse problems in which forward solves are expensive and PDE gradients are unavailable. The method is built on score-function estimators for the evidence lower bound (ELBO), which avoid differentiation through the PDE model but are known to suffer from high variance. To address this high variance, we employ multifidelity approximate control-variate estimators that combine a small number of high-fidelity samples with a larger number of low-fidelity samples to reduce estimator variance and the number of high-fidelity evaluations required for optimization. We further develop a PDE-derivative-free second-order optimization strategy based on both gradient and Hessian score-function estimators. For low-fidelity model generation, we propose an on-the-fly strategy that builds and adaptively updates a reduced-order model (ROM) as the variational distribution evolves throughout the optimization. We investigate strategies for adapting the ROM and estimating the approximate control-variate gains, examining tradeoffs between estimator bias, variance reduction, and computational cost. The resulting approach facilitates derivative-free variational inference for large-scale inverse problems through a reduction in overall computational cost. We demonstrate the method on four numerical examples: a linear benchmark with an exact posterior and three PDE-constrained inverse problems.

offered.title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
offered.abstract: Neural networks are commonly used to learn the solution operators of PDEs such as the Navier-Stokes equations and viscous conservation laws. On standard benchmarks, moderately sized and often shallow networks achieve small errors that decay at algebraic rates with the network size. These observations are not well described by the current approximation theory, which treats the solution operator as a generic map and derives worst-case bounds over large classes of operators. We show that the structure of the equations and their properties explain the observed behavior. For semilinear parabolic equations, the approximation costs separate into two terms, where one is controlled by an invariant of the governing law and the other by the data. The constitutive law can be parameterized as a single block whose size for accuracy $η$ is $O(η^{-pχ}\logη^{-1})$ for every $p>p_f$, where the structural exponent $p_f$ only depends on the computation graph of $f$. This exponent does not depend on the dimension and is in fact zero for polynomial laws, so for the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations the nonlinear block costs only $O(\logη^{-1})$ parameters. The data enters through encoding layers with a bounded number of learned weights per mode, so neither term grows with the grid resolution or the time step. While the analysis only uses the max-norm error of the pointwise block, we show that one obtains approximation bounds in a stronger norm along the whole trajectory. For viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a $C^s$ Hamiltonian, the approximation requires on the order of $η^{-1/s}$ parameters, and we prove a matching lower bound, up to logarithms. This shows that solution operators for this class of problems have low structural complexity, even though they are nonlinear maps between infinite-dimensional spaces.

offered.title: Random nodes with positive weights: Richter-Tchakaloff rules and optimal positive quadrature
offered.abstract: We show that independent random points support exact quadrature rules with positive weights.
